CI cost policy

Manual-only production opt-in CI for every hosted job to bound Actions spend.

About 2 min read · 1 sections

On this page
01 Local verification

Hosted GitHub Actions minutes for this repository are paused. The Mac-capable workflows were manually disabled on October 14, 2026, and the CI workflow now has no automatic triggers at all: keep everything paused until Edi explicitly requests a production build. This includes mixed workflows containing a Mac job: their Linux lanes are also paused while the workflow is disabled. Unaffected portable workflows remain unchanged.

The policy for .github/workflows/ci.yml:

  • Triggers: workflow_dispatch only. No push, pull_request, schedule, workflow_run, merge_group, or repository_dispatch entry may return.
  • Every hosted job — the Ubuntu verify job and the macOS macos-native job alike — carries a job-level guard requiring an explicit dispatch on refs/heads/production with the typed boolean run_build input set to true. run_build defaults to false, so a default dispatch allocates nothing.
  • macos-native additionally requires the typed boolean run_native opt-in, also defaulting to false. A branch push, tag push, production PR, schedule, or ordinary dispatch must not allocate a paid Mac or any other hosted runner.
  • Publication, where present, still needs its own affirmative publish input; a diagnostic is never a substitute for release verification.

Because all hosted builds are paused, local gates carry the day-to-day load: npm run build, npm run check, and npm test (plus the policy guards below) must pass before a change is considered validated.

Promote the reviewed workflow changes to production before requesting a build. Do not dispatch historical tags that contain old workflow definitions, rerun old paid jobs, or enable a workflow merely to check its configuration. The production workflow remains disabled_manually externally; the guards here must never be used to enable or dispatch it. Release/package workflows remain disabled after this change. Explicit production builds still incur normal GitHub charges; this is not a zero-dollar account cap.

Local verification

Run node --test scripts/tests/ci-native-policy.test.mjs and ruby scripts/test-ci-cost-policy.rb. Both parse the actual workflow YAML — the Node guard with its own parser and expression evaluator, the Ruby guard with the standard-library YAML parser — and check every hosted job against inline scenarios: automatic events with every opt-in, dispatches on wrong refs, missing or default opt-ins, and the positive production opt-in path. Each guard also mutates the parsed workflow (ungated Linux or new jobs, relaxed gates, added push/schedule triggers, run_build defaulting to true) and requires rejection. Where a production-release validator exists, the Ruby guard additionally exercises its tag identity checks. Configuration verification must not dispatch paid hosted jobs.
